t: Europe picks five countries for the Ukraine talks as Berlin warns Washington against surprises
x: Meeting in Dublin, European leaders entrusted their voice in future negotiations to the EU's institutions and to five members of the “coalition of the willing”. Germany's chancellor has asked Donald Trump for “no surprises” ahead of his expected talks with Vladimir Putin in China.

t: Qatar seals a defence pact with Turkey as Israel debates a strike on Iran
x: Doha and Ankara pledged on Friday to stand together against any armed attack on either of them, a sign of waning faith in America's guarantees in the Gulf. In Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu's caretaker government is preparing a fresh offensive against Iran, without open backing from the army or Washington.

t: A telecoms failure grounds every flight in America for more than four hours
x: The Federal Aviation Administration halted all take-offs nationwide on Friday after an outage hit air-traffic control centres. Thousands of flights were cancelled, and a return to normal could take several days.

t: The Houthis step up strikes on Saudi Arabia as the UN extends sanctions on Yemen
x: Riyadh says it intercepted drones over its capital and Eastern Province on Thursday, while Yemen's rebels claim attacks on oil and military sites. The Security Council has renewed sanctions on Yemen for another year.

t: In Burkina Faso, rival jihadists fight each other while the state fails to regain ground
x: Since September, Islamic State Sahel and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM have fought each other with rare ferocity near the Malian border. The junta, which has lost control of vast areas, is meanwhile tightening its crackdown on critics.

t: In Dublin, Volodymyr Zelensky announces a record prisoner swap and Europe's seat at the table
x: Ukraine's president says Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, whom he received on Thursday evening on their way back from the Kremlin, promised him the biggest prisoner exchange of the war. Europeans are expected to join the next round of talks, though Moscow has not confirmed it.

t: Iran says it hit an American radar in Bahrain as Donald Trump rules out a deal
x: The Revolutionary Guards claim to have destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday in retaliation for a strike on the port of Sirik, a claim America's military disputes. A day earlier America's president called a deal with Tehran unnecessary and took his vice-president off the file.

t: Dogged by suspicions of Chinese espionage, Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia's boss
x: The co-founder of the AI-chip giant resigned on Thursday, after revelations of an affair with a woman whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing. The chief financial officer, Colette Kress, takes over in the interim.
o: Nvidia and the China spying claims

t: Spain's first general strike since 2012 puts housing at the heart of the election
x: Hundreds of thousands marched through Spain's big cities on Wednesday, answering the main unions' call to protest against soaring rents and for higher wages. The mobilisation comes less than three weeks before the snap general election of 29 November.

t: In South Sudan, Amnesty accuses the UN and Juba of ignoring warnings before a massacre
x: The rights group says the authorities and UN peacekeepers knew an attack was being prepared on Abiemnom, where at least 213 people were killed on 1 March. The report comes six weeks before the first elections since independence.

t: After seeing Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump's envoys head to Dublin to meet Volodymyr Zelensky
x: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner spent more than two hours at the Kremlin on Thursday, with nothing announced on the substance of the conflict. Moscow says they backed a humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka.

t: Israel is reportedly readying a strike on Iran as two supertankers explode in Hormuz
x: Israel's security cabinet has reportedly ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack, according to the public broadcaster Kan. In Hormuz, the Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers were disabled by explosions.

t: Ebola in DR Congo passes 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,300 deaths
x: Figures published on Tuesday by the Congolese government confirm an outbreak of exceptional scale, the second-largest ever recorded. No vaccine or treatment is approved against the Bundibugyo strain.
o: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

t: At COP31, António Guterres urges world leaders to be done with fossil fuels
x: Addressing the leaders' summit in Antalya, the UN secretary-general said a temporary overshoot of 1.5°C was now inevitable. He wants an end to new coal, oil and gas projects.

t: In northern Tigray, Ethiopia's army and Eritrean forces are reported to be clashing around Badme
x: Having retaken most of Tigray in October, the federal army is pushing towards the Eritrean border. Addis Ababa accuses Asmara of invasion; Asmara calls that a pretext for war.

t: Russia and Ukraine agree a vast prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi, but no breakthrough
x: The American-brokered talks ended on Wednesday with an agreement in principle covering more than 1,000 prisoners on each side, according to Moscow. Nothing moved on territory, and America's envoys are expected at the Kremlin on Thursday.

t: France accuses Iran's Revolutionary Guards of sabotaging the fridges of 700 shops
x: France's foreign minister blames a cyber unit linked to the Guards for the attack on supermarkets on 12 October. Iran's ambassador has been summoned and Paris wants European sanctions.

t: Indonesia's vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, resigns amid doubts over his diplomas
x: The son of the former president Joko Widodo handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto on Wednesday, after court rulings found his school qualifications wanting. Parliament will then have 60 days to elect a successor.

t: In Haiti, Salvadoran troops destroy the house of the 400 Mawozo gang's leader
x: El Salvador's president, Nayib Bukele, on Tuesday claimed the assault on the gang's headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, where its leader was absent. American diplomats complain that El Salvador is acting without co-ordinating with the UN-backed force.

t: Niger has taken in nearly 64,000 refugees from Nigeria since January, says the UNHCR
x: Jihadist and criminal violence in northern Nigeria is driving tens of thousands of people into a drought-stricken neighbour. For lack of money, only 5% of the new arrivals have been registered.

t: In Abu Dhabi, Russians, Ukrainians and Americans reopen talks, with Europeans kept in the wings
x: Delegations from the three countries meet on Tuesday and Wednesday in the United Arab Emirates, together for the first time since February. The Europeans will be on hand, but Moscow refuses to let them join talks focused on security.

t: Kraków's Market Square gunman dies as terrorism investigators look for possible accomplices
x: The man behind Saturday's shooting, which killed six people in the city's historic heart, died in hospital on Monday. Prosecutors, who are treating it as terrorism, are now cautious about his ideological motives.

t: Nvidia investigates its boss, Jensen Huang, over ties to a woman suspected of spying for Beijing
x: The board of the AI-chip giant has handed an inquiry to independent directors after its chief executive's admission. Three House committee chairmen want to question him behind closed doors.
o: Nvidia and the China spying claims

t: South Africa's ANC suffers its worst setback as the big cities hunt for coalitions
x: Nelson Mandela's party won only about 31% of the vote in the local elections of 4 November, ahead of the Democratic Alliance. With no majority, several big cities, including Pretoria and Durban, will have to be run by coalitions.

t: In Yemen, at least 30 killed at a market near Taiz, with each side blaming the other
x: The Houthis accuse Saudi aircraft of bombing the Al-Hadara market on Friday; the recognised government blames Houthi missiles. According to the Yemen Data Project, October was the deadliest month for civilians since 2017.

t: Gadi Eisenkot accepts the mandate in Israel and calls for a national emergency government
x: The former army chief was formally asked on Sunday to form a government, with 67 recommendations but a bloc of only 48 members. He has invited Likud to join him and set four conditions for any partner.

t: Houthi attack damages an Aramco tower in the heart of Riyadh's financial district
x: Missiles fired from Yemen were intercepted over the Saudi capital on Sunday, but debris struck a building belonging to the oil giant. The Houthi authorities accuse Saudi aircraft of killing dozens of people near Sanaa.

t: In Ukraine 850,000 people lose power ahead of the talks in Abu Dhabi
x: Fresh Russian strikes hit the power grid on Sunday, notably in the Dnipropetrovsk region, and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power supply. Paris says Europeans will take part in the talks on 10 and 11 November.

t: COP31 opens in Antalya as the world looks set to overshoot 1.5°C
x: Nearly 200 countries meet in Turkey until 20 November for the UN climate conference, presided over by Ankara with Australia leading the negotiations. Current policies point to 2.8°C of warming, according to the UN's latest projection.

t: Myanmar's army kills eleven people in an air strike on a school in Sagaing
x: Teachers and children were among the victims of a bombing on Saturday in Kani township, according to independent Burmese media. The National Unity Government counted 641 army air strikes in October.

t: Isaac Herzog asks Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to form Israel's next government
x: On Saturday evening Israel's president gave the leader of Yashar, backed by 67 members of the Knesset, the job of building a coalition. Benjamin Netanyahu accuses his rival of wanting to govern with “supporters of terrorism”.

t: Iran lifts the range limit on its missiles after fresh American strikes in Hormuz
x: The Revolutionary Guards say they no longer observe a 2,000km ceiling on their ballistic missiles. Washington has set up a force to hunt down Iranian arms smuggling, as advisers urge Donald Trump to resume the war.

t: Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv three days before talks in Abu Dhabi
x: Overnight on 6-7 November Russia targeted the capital's power grid and damaged the North Bridge over the Dnipro. Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Moscow of preparing for negotiations “by launching ballistic missiles”.

t: Hoax bomb threats spread to European newsrooms after targeting dozens of flights
x: Ireland's public broadcaster, RTÉ, evacuated its offices on Friday after a threatening email, as did Bulgaria's Nova TV. Nearly 30 flights have been targeted since Tuesday, and no explosives have been found.

t: Haiti's 400 Mawozo gang reaches out to the state as Salvadoran troops close in
x: Wilson Joseph's gang says it has contacted the national disarmament commission and wants UN mediation. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, has announced the killing of a gang leader in Cité Soleil.

t: Paraguay's Santiago Peña is removed and confined to his home as Pedro Alliana takes over
x: The Senate on Friday removed the head of state, brought down by the collapse of Ueno bank, and his vice-president was sworn in at once. Prosecutors have ordered the former president to stay at home in an inquiry into suspected breach of trust and influence-peddling.

t: America strikes Iranian air defences in the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran vows to respond
x: Donald Trump confirmed on Friday evening “minor” strikes on an anti-aircraft system on Qeshm island, where Tehran says it shot down an American drone. Iran's army promises an “immediate” response, while Qatar denies that negotiations have failed.

t: Death toll from the Komyshuvakha strike passes 50 in Ukraine ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi
x: Ukraine's emergency services on Friday raised to at least 50 the death toll from the bombing of an aid centre in the Zaporizhzhia region. On the front line, Russia is barely advancing, according to the Institute for the Study of War.

t: Avigdor Liberman opens the door to the ultra-Orthodox on the eve of Isaac Herzog's choice
x: The leader of Yisrael Beiteinu says he is ready to govern with the ultra-Orthodox parties but rejects any government reliant on the Arab parties. Israel's president names the leader tasked with forming a government on Sunday.

t: Two new vaccines tested in DR Congo against an Ebola outbreak that has killed over 5,000
x: The WHO has added two vaccines designed against the Bundibugyo strain to the trial under way in Ituri. The outbreak, the worst in the country's history, has more than 10,500 confirmed cases.
o: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

t: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
x: Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.

t: Paraguay's Senate opens Santiago Peña's impeachment trial after his bid to resign fails
x: Congress was unable to accept the president's resignation on Thursday after his allies walked out, leaving it without a quorum. Senators began his trial on Friday, in his absence, over the collapse of the digital bank Ueno.

t: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, Russian and Ukrainian envoys meet at the White House
x: Melania Trump brought together envoys from both countries in Washington on Thursday, with no progress announced. On the ground, Moscow is targeting Ukraine's energy and logistics networks while Kyiv steps up drone attacks on Russian refineries.

t: Herzog to name Israel's next prime minister on Sunday, with Gadi Eisenkot in pole position
x: With 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset behind him, the former army chief awaits the mandate the president is due to hand out on 8 November. In Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, down to 46 backers, some cry "stolen" election.

t: Somalia's Supreme Court rules the extension of the president's term unlawful
x: The country's highest court on Thursday gave the parties thirty days to reach agreement and ninety days to hold elections. The day before, the head of state, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, had sacked the chief justice.

t: Midterms: Democrats retake Congress as Trump pays the price for the Iran war
x: After a historic election night, the opposition has seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The president admits that the conflict with Tehran weighed heavily on the vote.

t: Washington and Tehran: fears of a return to war after the US vote
x: Qatar is trying to secure an interim deal before the United States resumes its strikes. Eight months into the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains almost closed and oil is above $100 a barrel.

t: Russia strikes civilians and the power grid in Ukraine ahead of new talks
x: A Russian strike on a school where humanitarian aid was being handed out has killed at least 43 people in the Zaporizhzhia region, as Moscow keeps pounding the power grid. Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

t: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot wins the backing of most MPs against Benjamin Netanyahu
x: Abandoned by the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party, Benjamin Netanyahu gathers only 46 recommendations, against 67 for his rival, who is backed by the Arab parties. In Gaza, a year after the ceasefire, Israeli strikes still claim lives almost every day.

t: In Sudan, a drone war is strangling civilians
x: More than three years into the conflict, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are stepping up strikes on infrastructure. The crisis is now spilling over into neighbouring Ethiopia.

t: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

x: The United Nations, founded in 1945, which has 193 member states.
The UN body responsible for peace: fifteen members, five of them permanent (Britain, China, France, Russia, America) with a veto.
A military alliance founded in 1949 between European and North American countries: an attack on one is treated as an attack on all (Article 5).
The International Atomic Energy Agency, a UN body in Vienna that inspects nuclear programmes.
The UN office that co-ordinates emergency humanitarian aid and compiles crisis tolls.
The UN agency that protects refugees and displaced people.
The World Food Programme, the UN agency for emergency food aid.
The International Committee of the Red Cross, an independent Swiss organisation that protects and assists victims of armed conflict.
The UN agency that tracks migration and population displacement.
People forced from their homes who remain inside their own country, unlike refugees, who have crossed a border.
An agreement under which warring parties suspend fighting, without settling the conflict itself.
The encirclement of a territory or its ports to stop it trading or being resupplied.
Measures against a country, company or person to pressure its policy: asset freezes, trade or travel bans.
North Sea crude oil whose price is the benchmark for much of the oil traded worldwide.
The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, which co-ordinates its members’ output to influence prices.
The European Central Bank, in Frankfurt, which sets interest rates for the euro zone.
The rate at which a central bank lends to banks: raising it curbs inflation, cutting it supports activity.
A general, lasting rise in prices that erodes the purchasing power of money.
Israel’s parliament, a single chamber of 120 members: 61 votes are needed to govern.
The lower chamber of America’s Congress: 435 members, all re-elected every two years.
American elections held two years into a presidential term: the whole House of Representatives and a third of the Senate are re-elected.
A procedure by which a parliament can remove a head of state from office.
The minimum number of members who must be present for an assembly to vote validly.
An alliance of several parties that pool their seats to win a majority and govern together.
A Palestinian Islamist movement that seized control of the Gaza Strip in 2007; its attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 set off the Gaza war.
A Lebanese Shia movement, both political party and armed militia, backed by Iran.
Yemeni rebels backed by Iran, who seized Sanaa, the capital, in 2014.
Palestinian territory west of the Jordan river, occupied by Israel since 1967.
A narrow Palestinian territory of about 365 square kilometres on the Mediterranean, bordering Israel and Egypt.
The sea passage between Iran and Oman through which about a fifth of the world’s oil consumption passes.
The Rapid Support Forces, Sudanese paramilitaries led by General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemedti”, at war with the army since April 2023.
A government that took power in a coup and is run by military officers.
The annual conference of the parties to the UN climate convention, where pledges against global warming are negotiated.
A climate accord adopted in 2015 that aims to keep warming well below 2°C, and if possible 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels.
Commitments by which countries promise to defend a state if it is attacked again.
The highest authority in the Islamic Republic of Iran, above the president; he commands the armed forces.
The Islamic Republic of Iran’s ideological army, separate from the regular army, with its own ground, naval and missile forces.
An often fatal viral haemorrhagic fever spread by contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person or animal.
